summary: Category and collection product grid with filters and pagination. System section of the category page; the search page shows a child copy of it.
rules: Always write the filter position: `filters.position` in the current settings, the root `filtersPosition` in a section stored at settings version 1791195496953 or older (`presets apply` picks the key by the section's version; the other one is ignored or dropped). Left out, it is `inline`: a left sidebar (category tree, price, stock, Apply/Reset) that takes about a quarter of the width, which settings get without anyone choosing it. `drawer` is a filter button over the grid.

Page size is rows × columns (rows 3-6, columns 2-6); there is no other count. `snippets.layout` picks how more products load: `grid` (the default) numbers the pages, `feed` adds the next page as the shopper scrolls (search robots still get numbered pages). The sample predates `feed`, so the presets leave `layout` as the store has it. Sorting, the H1 and the category description are not settings: keep the H1 short in the cabinet.

`filters.enableAutoApply` applies a filter as soon as it changes and drops the Apply button (Reset stays); `filters.enableChips` shows the chosen filters as chips above the grid. Both are off by default. The sample predates them, so there is no count behind either: the presets leave them as the store has them, and a section older than the `filters` settings cannot carry them.

`snippet.enableButton: disabled` hides card buttons whatever the theme says, `enabled` forces them, `default` follows the theme's `buttonColorInListing`. The presets write `default`: buttons are the theme card's decision, shared with the shelves.
The card look (photo ratio, order, plate) is the theme's `productSnippet`: it also changes every shelf, so change it only with the merchant's agreement.
The search-page listing is a child copy in most stores: edits change both. Tell the user before editing.
The Split and Yandex points lines (`snippet.yandexSplit`, `snippet.yandexDiscount`) are the store's configuration: presets never write them.

presets.name: listing-drawer-4x6
presets.use: Default category page: filters in a drawer, 4 columns, 24 per page, no card buttons. Packshots on a plate or mixed photography.
presets.evidence: a 4-column drawer listing in about 1 in 3 stores; 24 per page in about 2 in 5. One shared starter listing inflates the raw counts: about 17 independent listing decisions stand behind 42 listings

presets.name: listing-large-cards-3col
presets.use: Portrait 3:4 model photography, small and medium assortments: 3 columns, 18 per page.
presets.evidence: 18 per page in about 1 in 3 stores; 3 columns with 3:4 photos in about 3 in 10

presets.name: listing-inline-filters
presets.use: Opt-in marketplace listing for large assortments filtered by price and stock first: the inline sidebar, 3 columns because it takes a quarter of the width, card buttons following the theme.
presets.evidence: the sidebar renders in about 1 in 4 stores, half of them by accident (settings without a filter position); most stores with card buttons in the listing use it

presets.name: listing-gallery-5col-gapless
presets.use: Gallery wall for small objects when every photo shares one plate: 5 columns, no gaps. Never with mixed backgrounds.
